section_summary: This section comprises monthly reports on conditions in Japan (Reports Nos. 40 through 46) submitted by the American Embassy in Tokyo to the Department of State between February and August 1930, under Ambassador William R. Castle, Jr. and Chargé d'Affaires Edwin L. Neville. The despatches document critical economic, political, and international developments, including the lifting of the gold embargo, worsening industrial depression, widespread labor unrest and strikes (notably at General Motors and Kanegafuchi Spinning Company), the celebration marking the post-earthquake reconstruction of Tokyo, and proceedings of the Imperial Diet. External affairs feature prominently, encompassing the London Naval Conference and subsequent naval staff crisis, the Sino-Japanese Tariff Agreement, and contentious fishery and territorial disputes with Soviet Russia.

subfiles.about: Transmits Embassy Report No. 40 on political, labor, and financial conditions in Japan during January 1930, together with lists of despatches and telegrams sent to the Department.
subfiles.from: W. R. Castle, Jr., American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Reviews the lifting of the gold embargo on January 11, 1930, resulting in substantial gold exports, and notes that domestic financial stability was preserved through untouched foreign credits. Details labor unrest at General Motors Japan in Osaka following dismissals, including an appeal to the Embassy by proletarian leader Ikuo Oyama, contrasting with a daily minimum wage increase enacted by Ford at Yokohama. Reports a record retirement allowance of Yen 3,000,000 granted to Sanji Muto of Kanegafuchi Spinning Company and mentions the impending release of the assassin of former Prime Minister Takashi Hara. Appends comprehensive schedules of despatches and telegrams sent to the Department of State throughout January 1930.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 22: Transmitting Report on Conditions in Japan for January 1930 (Report No. 40)

subfiles.about: Transmits Embassy Report No. 41 on political, international, and commercial conditions in Japan during February 1930, along with lists of despatches and telegrams.
subfiles.from: W. R. Castle, Jr., American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Chronicles the national general elections of February 20, 1930, which completely dominated public and political attention in Japan throughout the month. Summarizes the meeting of the Toa Chosakai (Council of Inquiry into Far Eastern Affairs) chaired by Count Kiyoura, which passed resolutions concerning Chinese communications, extraterritoriality, anti-foreign agitations, and Japanese fishery rights in Soviet waters. Reviews a public address in Tokyo by the Soviet Vice Trade Representative detailing expanding bilateral trade, oil and timber concessions, and Soviet demands for extended commercial credit terms. Concludes with complete schedules of despatches and telegrams forwarded during February 1930, focusing heavily on disarmament proposals and election returns.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 66: Transmitting Report on Conditions in Japan for February 1930 (Report No. 41)

subfiles.about: Transmits Embassy Report No. 42 on conditions in Japan for March 1930, focusing on earthquake reconstruction celebrations, severe economic depression, and government relief policies.
subfiles.from: W. R. Castle, Jr., American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Describes the elaborate civic and imperial ceremonies held on March 27, 1930, marking the formal completion of the reconstruction of Tokyo following the catastrophic 1923 earthquake. Contrasts the festive celebrations with deepening domestic economic distress, rising unemployment among both manual laborers and university graduates, and Cabinet debates over industrial rationalization. Analyzes proposed state interventions, including raw silk price compensation, rice market regulation, credit assistance for small businesses, and expanded central government subsidies for primary school teachers' salaries. Mentions preliminary diplomatic developments, such as the initialing of a tariff agreement with China, Indian cotton duties, and the bribery indictment of former Education Minister Mitsue Kobashi, accompanied by monthly schedules of despatches and telegrams.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 91: Transmitting Report on Conditions in Japan for March 1930 (Report No. 42)

subfiles.about: Transmits Embassy Report No. 43 on political, economic, and labor developments in Japan during April 1930, alongside monthly schedules of telegrams and despatches.
subfiles.from: Edwin L. Neville, Counselor of Embassy (For the Ambassador), Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Reports on the convening of the 58th Diet session, preliminary court findings in Tokyo municipal corruption scandals and ministry bribery cases, and the Privy Council's approval of the Sino-Japanese Tariff Agreement. Focuses on significant labor conflicts, detailing the widespread walkout of 40,000 workers at Kanegafuchi Spinning Company over bonus reductions following Sanji Muto's departure, as well as municipal transportation strikes in Tokyo and Kobe. Notes administrative measures to alleviate economic stagnation, including the establishment of an International Tourist Bureau under the Department of Railways and a Trade Bureau in the Department of Commerce and Industry. Includes monthly schedules of despatches and telegrams covering London Naval Treaty developments, opium control, and the laying of the cornerstone for the new American Embassy.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 127: Transmitting Report on Conditions in Japan for April 1930 (Report No. 43)

subfiles.about: Transmits Embassy Report No. 44 on political, labor, and social conditions in Japan for May 1930, together with lists of despatches and telegrams sent to Washington.
subfiles.from: Edwin L. Neville, Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Covers the conclusion of the extraordinary Diet session, the promulgation of the Sino-Japanese Tariff Agreement, and escalating friction between the Cabinet and the Naval General Staff regarding the London Naval Treaty. Details criminal indictments handed down in the Decorations Scandal involving the Board of Decorations, the resignation of Tokyo Mayor Zenjiro Horikiri over municipal political friction, and ongoing labor disputes at Kanegafuchi mills alongside orderly May Day rallies. Mentions cultural and social incidents, including Japan's victory in the Ninth Far Eastern Championship Games, the ritual suicide (seppuku) of a naval officer, and a notable charitable donation in Kobe. Submits supporting schedules of telegrams and despatches regarding treaty interpretations, Ambassador Castle's departure, and embassy construction progress.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 163: Transmitting Report on Conditions in Japan for May 1930 (Report No. 44)

subfiles.about: Transmits Embassy Report No. 45 on political, naval, labor, and diplomatic events in Japan during June 1930, including schedules of despatches and telegrams.
subfiles.from: Edwin L. Neville, Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Highlights the political fallout of the London Naval Treaty, marked by the resignation of Chief of Naval Staff Admiral Kanji Kato and the return of chief delegate Reijiro Wakatsuki to Tokyo. Summarizes the final negotiated settlement of the prolonged 55-day strikes across the Kanegafuchi Spinning Company mills, Communist arrests in Karafuto, the deportation of a Soviet trade employee, and maritime tensions resulting from the Soviet seizure of Japanese fishing vessels including the crab cannery Mikuni Maru. Details the decision to locate the Showa Steel Works at Anshan in Manchuria, the selection of Hidejiro Nagata as Mayor of Tokyo, and the formal accreditation of Persia's first diplomatic envoy to Japan, H. L. Mossaed. Contains lists of despatches and telegrams sent during June 1930 concerning treaty ratification delays and diplomatic appointments, including that of W. Cameron Forbes.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 187: Transmitting Report on Conditions in Japan for June 1930 (Report No. 45)

subfiles.about: Transmits Embassy Report No. 46 on political and economic conditions in Japan during July 1930, focusing on industrial rationalization and severe budget deficits.
subfiles.from: Edwin L. Neville, Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Analyzes the intensifying nationwide economic depression and comprehensive private and governmental discussions regarding the rationalization of major Japanese industries. Details plans initiated by Tokyo syndicate bank leaders, led by Seihin Ikeda of Mitsui, to organize cooperative credit investigation machinery, alongside rationalization proposals for steel, shipbuilding, wool, and cement cartels. Reviews proposals to lower state railway freight rates to ease production costs and examines severe budgetary dilemmas facing the government due to an anticipated ¥60,000,000 drop in tax revenues for the upcoming fiscal year. Note that this document's text breaks off at page 80 and continues into subsequent pages of the original file.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 219: Transmitting Report on Conditions in Japan for July 1930 (Report No. 46) [Incomplete]
